doc.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The trio at Chess and The In Crowd
title: Daddy-O Daylie takes the trio to Chess Records
summary: Playing Stelzer's, the trio is told by Daddy-O Daylie to make a record and is introduced to Phil and Leonard Chess.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, nightclubs. London House, Kelly’s, many places to play. But we ended up playing at Stelzer’s. Stelzer’s was a restaurant on this side, bar on this side, and in the bar, they had music. They hired us to be a trio. While we were there, Daddy-O heard us again. He said, “You guys are pretty good.” “Thank you.” He says, “You should make a record.” He introduced us to Phil and Leonard Chess. I’m trying to – I think by now Redd is out of the army, because he’s on that first album. Also, we’re playing 4, 5, 6 nights a week. Things are getting better for us in many, many ways. But it was when Daddy-O Daylie introduced us to the Chess brothers and Phil
auditioned us and eventually we made our first album, that things began to get much better.
